summary: George Chemparathy was a scholar of Indology and philosophy who studied under Erich Frauwallner and Paul Hacker. He held posts at Loyola College, Chennai, and served as a professor at Utrecht University from circa 1974 to 1993.

George Christopher Molesworth Birdwood worked in Indology and history/archaeology after earning an M.D. at the University of Edinburgh (~1850-1854). He held posts at Grant Medical College (~1858-1868), Government Museum, Chennai, and the India Office (1878-1899).

George Cowgill was an archaeologist and historian who studied at Stanford University (~1948-1952) and Harvard University (~1956-1963). He held academic posts at Brandeis University (~1964-1990) and Arizona State University (~1990-2013).

George Croom Robertson was a philosopher who studied at the University of Aberdeen (~1857-1861) and University College London (~1862-1863). He subsequently held a post at University College London from circa 1866 to 1892.

George Cœdès worked in history, archaeology, Indology, and linguistics, studying at EPHE under Alfred Foucher, Louis Finot, and Sylvain Lévi. He directed the École française d'Extrême-Orient (1929-1947) and served as conservator at the National Library of Thailand (1918-1929).

George D. Bond is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who earned his PhD at Northwestern University (~1968-1972) and studied at the University of Sri Lanka. He served as Professor of Religion at Northwestern University (~1974-2012).

George David Birkhoff studied at the University of Chicago and Harvard University. His career included academic posts at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (1907-1909), Princeton University (1909-1912), and Harvard University (1912-1944).
George Ernest Ward worked in Indology and linguistics. He completed his higher education at Oxford, studying at The Queen's College and Wadham College (~1856-1860).

George Eugene Dunkel specialized in linguistics and Indology, studying at the University of Pennsylvania and under Karl Hoffmann. He held posts at Johns Hopkins University (1975-1978), Princeton University (1978-1986), and the University of Zurich (appointed 1986).

George Everest studied at the Royal Military Academy, Woolwich (~1804-1806). Active in Indology and related fields, he served as an assistant with the Great Trigonometrical Survey (1817) and Surveyor General of the Survey of India (1830-1843).

George F. Dales, a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology, earned his PhD at the University of Pennsylvania. He held posts at the Royal Ontario Museum, University of Toronto, University of Pennsylvania, and UC Berkeley (appointed 1972).
George Fletcher MacMunn studied at the Royal Military Academy, Woolwich in 1888. Active in history, archaeology, and Indology, he served as Warden of Sackville College from 1939 to 1952.

George Foot Moore, a religious studies scholar, studied at Yale University and Union Theological Seminary. He was a professor at Andover Theological Seminary (1883-1902) and held professorships at Harvard University, including the Frothingham chair (1904-1928).

George Frederick Nicholl worked in Indology and linguistics, earning his M.A. from Balliol College, Oxford. He served as Lecturer in Oriental Languages at Oxford (1878-1909) and Professor of Sanskrit and Persian at King's College London (appointed 1879).
George Gordon Rogers was an Indologist and linguist who completed his studies at Bedford College and the Royal Military Academy Sandhurst (~1912-1913).

George Henry Rouse was a scholar of religious studies and Indology. He studied at Regent's Park College (~1856-1860) and the University of London (~1858-1861), later teaching at Haverfordwest Baptist College (1867-1872).
George Herbert Palmer was a philosopher who studied at Phillips Academy and Harvard University (~1860-1864). He subsequently held an academic post at Harvard University from circa 1870 to 1913.
George Herbert Westcott was an Indology and religious studies scholar who studied at Peterhouse, Cambridge (1882-1885). In 1894, he held a post as a Fellow at the University of Allahabad.

George L. Hart, a scholar of Indology and linguistics, earned his PhD at Harvard under Daniel H. H. Ingalls. He taught Sanskrit at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (~1969-1975) before serving as professor at UC Berkeley (~1975-2011).

George Lakoff, a linguist and philosopher, studied at MIT, Indiana University Bloomington, and under Roman Jakobson. He taught linguistics at Harvard University (1965-1969) and was a professor of linguistics at UC Berkeley from 1972 to 2016.
